TASK: pass 2 of the motion/animation/effects asset program for Cyrus. The owner wants MANY more effects, motions and animations, CC0 ONLY (the owner will not show creator credit, so CC-BY is excluded: tier must be cc0 with attribution null; CC-BY and 'attribution required' sources are rejected), and wants everything cataloged with as many TOKEN-FREE scripts as possible (spend as little as possible: use deterministic scripts for every conversion, measurement, tagging and cataloging step; no model calls per asset). Token-economical, no sub-agents. READ FIRST: /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/S-motion-assets.md (pass 1 results and gaps: water, doors/mechanisms, car doors and every effect preset missing; 30 CC0 FBX files with 94 clip stacks need conversion; itch.io CC0 VFX packs unverified), R-motion-effects.md (formats the Motion core consumes: glTF animation clips, particle presets as parameter JSON, flipbook sprite sheets), and the staged data under /tank/cyrus-library-staging/motion/ (your subtree; do NOT touch /tank/cyrus-library-staging/catalog.jsonl or other agents' files; write only to motion/ and its own catalog file motion/catalog-motion-2.jsonl + motion/LICENCE-LEDGER-motion-2.csv).

DO, in this order: (1) CONVERT the 30 CC0 FBX files to glb with a deterministic script using the already-downloaded headless Blender (/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/blender-poc on node-2; run via the same sandbox recipe as /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/I-blender-poc.md: systemd-run, no network, caps, build lock, one job at a time) or another licence-clean converter you verify; validate each glb (gltf-validator if available), extract clip names/durations/frame counts with a script, add rows (kind animation-clip / animated-model) to catalog-motion-2.jsonl with deterministic tags derived from file/pack/clip names (walk, run, idle, attack, fire, reload, slide, die...). (2) PROCEDURAL GENERATORS (we author, so no licence issue, zero per-asset tokens): write deterministic Python/numpy (or node) scripts that generate flipbook sprite sheets with alpha: fire (several styles), smoke (light/dark/black), explosion (several sizes), water splash and ripple, sparks, muzzle flash (several), dust puff, impact hit, magic glow/aura (several colours), electric arc, blood-free impact sparks, steam, snow/rain streak, and tileable water/lava/fire loop textures; 64/128/256 px frames, power-of-two sheets, seeds recorded, each with a JSON sidecar (frames, grid, fps, loop, blend mode hint, tags); target at least 150 sheets via parameter variation. Save under motion/procedural/, rows with tier cc0 (source 'nxeon-procedural', licence 'CC0-1.0, authored by Nxeon', no attribution), a contact-sheet PNG of each family under /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/motion-sheets-procedural/ so the owner can SEE them (look at them yourself and fix ugly families). (3) MORE CC0 SOURCES: verify (read and quote the licence page) and stage clean CC0 animation clips, flipbooks, particle textures and VFX packs from: itch.io CC0 VFX/animation packs (only verifiable ones), OpenGameArt CC0 effects, Kenney animation/particle kits not yet staged, Quaternius CC0 animated packs (NOT the new Bestiary kit under the 2026-08-28 QAL licence), other large CC0 collections. Reject Mixamo-style, NC, ND, attribution-required, unlicensed. Dedupe by sha256 against motion/ and the main catalog. (4) TOKEN-FREE CATALOGING: for every row you add also write deterministic tags/categories/useFor via scripts (reuse lib/cyrus/library/v2 vocabularies: read /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r2/lib/cyrus/library/v2/ for the controlled tags and situations, add effect/motion vocabulary entries as a proposed JSON file motion/vocabulary-proposal.json rather than editing the repo). (5) Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/S2-motion-assets.md (under 700 words, tables): what was converted, generated and added (counts by kind), licence evidence, what the owner can now cover (explosion, fire, water splash/flow, smoke, muzzle flash, door/mechanism, gun cocking, creature walk/attack) and what still must be authored as MotionSpec presets by the Motion core, disk used.

LIMITS/RULES: staging only under /tank/cyrus-library-staging/motion/ (never git, never the root disk /: TMPDIR=/tank/cyrus-library-staging/tmp-motion, nice -n 19 ionice -c3, one download/job at a time, +50 GB cap, stop if / has <8G free); never edit/build in /opt/nxeon or /opt/nxeon-staging; no repo changes; no paid sources or accounts; never git add -A; NEVER pkill by pattern (kill by PID only); do not touch VM 88001, production or customer VMs. Final reply to the parent: at most 150 words.

# I: Headless Blender code-modelling PoC (Cyrus L4 route a)

Run 2026-10-10 on node-2, workspace `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/blender-poc/`. One agent, no sub-agents, no paid APIs. Sources in `blender-poc/src/` (harness.py, sbx.sh logic, prop scripts per round). Renders and glbs in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/blender-poc/` (glbs in `out/`).

## Setup (VERIFIED)
- Blender **5.2.2 LTS** (current LTS per blender.org/download/lts) portable tarball, sha256 `84098912...a168` matched the file published at download.blender.org. Never installed system-wide.
- Run only as `blender --background --factory-startup --python harness.py -- prop.py name`.
- Sandbox: a transient systemd unit in `nxeon-build-agents.slice` holding the node-2 build lock (same properties as run-capped.sh plus extras). I called systemd-run directly because `devhost` insists on a git worktree of the repo, which would have changed the repo.
- Extras: `PrivateNetwork=yes` (no network), User=nobody, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `/opt /tank /var/lib /mnt` replaced by empty tmpfs apart from the Blender dir (read-only) and a work dir, MemoryMax 4G, CPUQuota 400%, TasksMax 256, RuntimeMax, no capabilities, NoNewPrivileges.
- Renderer: Cycles CPU, 32 spp, denoise, 640x480 (crate) / 768x480 (rifle), 3 views + contact sheet. EEVEE not tried (no GPU). Three.js/Playwright render of the glb: **not done (UNVERIFIED)**; glb checked via Blender re-import and Khronos gltf-validator instead.
- Harness prelude (`mat`, `box`, `cyl`, `prism`, join-by-material, smart_project, export, render) is fixed code I wrote once. It is effectively a tiny parts kit, so per-prop scripts are shorter than a cold start would be.

## Results per prop
| | Crate (A) | Rifle (B) |
|---|---|---|
| Rounds used | 3 of 6 | 4 of 6 |
| Wall per round | 26-28 s (render ~21 s inside Blender, rest ssh/scp) | 26 s |
| Triangles (final) | 6,720 | 2,732 |
| Objects after join by material | 5 (64 before) | 3 |
| Per-object non-manifold edges (bmesh) | 0 | 0 |
| UV present | yes, all objects (smart_project) | yes |
| glb valid | validator: 0 errors, 0 warnings; Blender re-import tri count equal | same |
| glb size | 476 KB | 187 KB |
| Quality vs intent | **7.5/10** | **6.5/10** |
| Est. tokens | ~15k (UNVERIFIED, from session counter) | ~20k |

Quality is my own judgement from the renders. The crate reads as a sci-fi supply crate: panels, ribs, chunky corner caps, latches, end handles, glowing strip. The rifle is recognisably AK-pattern in side, 3/4 and top views: curved magazine, slanted grip, gas tube, wood furniture, muzzle brake, front sight. It looks stylised-blocky and flat-shaded with no wear or textures.

## Round log (renders: `<prop>-r<N>-<3q|side|back|top>.png`, sheet `<prop>-r<N>-sheet.png`)
| Round | What changed |
|---|---|
| crate-r1 | First script. Pale and overexposed; read as a filing cabinet; glow strip hidden behind a panel. |
| crate-r2 | Darker palette, chunky corner caps, ribbed panels, yellow label, glow moved in front of the panel, handles moved up. Reads as a crate. |
| crate-r3 (final) | Darker lid, saturated glow, lid ribs, join by material, exposure -0.9. (The exposure change reached node-2 only for r3; r1 and r2 were rendered at exposure 0 because my sync script forgot harness.py.) |
| rifle-r1 | First script. Already recognisable; mag thin, wood pale, trigger guard a full ring. |
| rifle-r2 | Darker wood, U-shaped trigger guard, fatter mag and grip, butt plate, trunnion. |
| rifle-r3 | Added cover ribs and handguard grooves. The cover ribs looked like a rail comb (a regression). |
| rifle-r4 (final) | Removed cover ribs, kept grooves. |
Final sheets: `crate-final-sheet.png`, `rifle-final-sheet.png`.

## What failed or was weak (VERIFIED from renders)
- First attempts have wrong proportions, colours and exposure. Most gains came from looking at the picture (hidden glow strip, regression from the cover ribs); the numeric checks alone caught none of them.
- "Manifold" is per closed shell. Parts overlap and are not boolean-unioned, so the mesh is not one watertight solid. Interior faces are wasted triangles.
- Rifle details are cuboid and cylinder primitives. Organic curves (stock, grip) are crude. Texturing is flat colours only; no normal bake or LOD was attempted.
- 1 m scale holds (bbox 1.03 m rifle; crate 1.14 x 0.70 x 0.65 m including handles and feet).

## Safety (sandbox probes VERIFIED)
A model-written script runs full Python inside Blender: `os`, `subprocess`, `socket`, file access, `bpy.ops.wm.url_open`.
| Probe | Result in sandbox |
|---|---|
| connect to 1.1.1.1, DNS, curl subprocess | blocked (no network namespace) |
| read /root, /etc/shadow, other pids' environ | permission denied |
| list /opt, /etc/nxeon-build, /var/lib, /home | empty |
| write /etc, /usr, /tank | read-only filesystem |
| write to work dir; run `id` | allowed; uid 65534 |
| `while True`, 100 MB allocation loop, fork bomb | killed at the timeout; killed by OOM in 4 s; contained by TasksMax and timeout. No units left behind. |
Not verified: kernel-exploit escapes (a systemd unit is not a VM). The real worker needs a stronger boundary (gVisor, microVM, or an allow-list that rejects `import os/subprocess/socket` before running) plus the same no-network and cap properties. Pre-run static rejection and the sandbox should both be used.

## Cost
About 5k tokens per round (script 1.5-2.5k output, image read ~2k, stats 0.5k), 3-4 rounds, so roughly 15-20k tokens per finished prop here with a fixed prelude. A cold start without the prelude, or props 3-5x more complex, would be higher; I did not measure that. Compute is about 25 s of 4 CPU threads per round. A customer price must cover: tokens x rounds (and retries that end in rejection), CPU seconds, human fix time, and the risk of failed or rejected jobs. I cannot back a dollar figure without current token pricing and failure rates.

## Recommendation
- **GO for the code-modelling route for stylised hard-surface props** (crates, lanterns, simplified guns) as a "draft for a human to fix". Not a GO for hero or realistic assets, organic shapes, or likeness.
- A **parts kit** (bevelled box, panel, handle, cylinder, curved-profile prism, join and UV, material presets, camera and light rig) would cut tokens per round, lock scale and conventions, and make failures less likely. Add a union-then-cleanup pass so the output is closer to one watertight mesh.
- Measure next: (1) 20+ varied prompts, success rate at <=4 rounds, tokens per success; (2) a vision-model "look" step instead of me, and how often it catches regressions like rifle-r3; (3) boolean union, decimate to `meshBudget`, LOD and bake time; (4) in-engine load (three.js/FiveM) and texture quality; (5) the stronger sandbox; (6) a blind rating of "not cheap" by the owner.

1. CC-BY tier: accept the 9 CC-BY sheets (attribution page needed) or drop them. The Soluna pack can be treated as CC0 if you accept the dual-listing.

3. FBX to glTF: approve installing a converter (or a node FBXLoader script) in an isolated place so the 30 creature and gun FBX files become glb.
4. MIT or Apache preset repos (such as tsparticles) were not staged because only CC0/CC-BY is allowed; say if permissive licences are acceptable for effect presets.
5. itch.io CC0 VFX packs: hand-pick a few if you want more fire and explosion variety.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or for an HTML or Markdown page to view or share. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save. A page declares these through the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of this would make the page more useful, Claude must load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code.** Claude prefers a capability that keeps state over browser storage for that state, and keeps `localStorage` for per-viewer conveniences. Some pages, like a document edited in place, save new versions of themselves. Such a save reaches this session like any other republish, as a notice on a watched artifact or a conflict on Claude's next publish, and Claude then re-reads the page, merges the changes and republishes.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Claude always authors the page as `.html`, and publishes a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly asks for one. When the person shares a Markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, Claude builds an HTML page from its content, keeping its substance and designing the page as it would any other artifact rather than transcribing the Markdown one to one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB work, but each artifact has its own origin and what a page stores lives only in that viewer's browser. It survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices or Claude. It can come back empty, or the accessor can throw, in a private window, with cleared or blocked site data, in previews or during thumbnail capture, so Claude wraps every read and write in try/catch and makes the page render correctly without it. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

ampler must be pure (time in, pose out) so screenshots are reproducible (U).

## 3. Per-game animation systems (go/no-go for AI generation)

| Game | Format / toolchain | Server can deliver? | AI gen | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minecraft | display entities, `.mcmeta`, item states, BetterModel clips | Yes (pack + plugin) | Yes (parametric) | GO now |
| Hytale | `.blockyanim` (keyframes pos/rot/scale), attached via `CustomModelAnimation`; Blockbench Hytale plugin; JSON schema not published in what we read | Asset packs; plugin triggers (Takedown plugin exists) | Likely (JSON) once a real file is diffed | LATER (V hytalemodding.dev animated-block-textures, creating-block; schema U) |
| FiveM / RedM | anim dictionaries `.ycd` in `stream/`, played with `RequestAnimDict`+`TaskPlayAnim`; vehicle doors/bones, ptfx assets (`.ypt`), via natives (door natives and ptfx native names U) | Yes, `stream/` is server-streamed | Reuse existing dict/clip names = easy; authoring new ycd needs CodeWalker/Sollumz (no-licence / GPL) | GO as "pick from existing dictionaries + ptfx presets"; NO-GO for authoring new ycd (V docs.fivem.net TASK_PLAY_ANIM_ADVANCED; wiki.gtaconnected requestAnims; rest U) |
| Source / GMod | QC `$sequence`, SMD/DMX, studiomdl; PCF particles (V developer.valvesoftware.com) | Workshop `.gma` | Medium; compile needs Windows + game | LATER |
| Palworld / ARK (Unreal) | AnimSequence/Montage/Niagara cooked into pak; pak mods usually need each client to install; UE4SS mods not usable on dedicated servers (V indifferentbroccoli wiki, nexusmods) | Palworld no; ASA via CurseForge ID | Low (cook toolchain) | NO-GO |
| Unturned (Unity) | AnimationClips in master bundle via MasterBundleTool; gun clips Equip/Reload/Hammer/etc. (V docs.smartlydressedgames.com via search) | Workshop auto-download | Medium, needs Unity editor | LATER |

## 4. AI feasibility

| Reliable (Claude) | Not reliable |
|---|---|
| Parametric gaits (walk/run: phase, stride, bob, swing amplitudes per archetype), as already done by creature templates | Mocap-quality human motion, nuanced acting, retargeted dance |
| Mechanical motion: hinges, slides, recoil kicks, slide/bolt cycles, wheel spin, with eased keyframes | Free-form quadruped/creature gaits without a template |
| State machines and trigger wiring (events to sound/particle/light) | Frame-accurate timing by ear (needs human nudge against the waveform) |
| Particle presets by parameters (count, speed, spread, colour ramp, lifetime) | Photoreal fire/water |

Cheapest approach: preset library (kind `motion`/`effect`) + generators with a few typed knobs + AI picks/parameterises/composes + human fixes in the studio timeline. Always validate against caps and show a simulated preview before export (U, consistent with how designer/ and creature/ already work).

## 5. Recommended architecture

**Motion core (game-neutral, pure TS, Zod, like RigSpec/designer):** `MotionSpec v1 { clips[], machines[], rig?, caps }`.
- Track kinds: `transform` (target node, channel pos/rot/scale, keys with ease), `particle` (preset ref + params + emitter node + start/duration), `sound-cue` (sound id from Sound Studio, tick, gain/pitch), `light-material` (emissive/colour/opacity/texture-frame), `event` (named marker, state transition).
- Time in integer ticks at 20 Hz canonical, fractional allowed; exporters resample (Minecraft 1 tick, Hytale fps, Source/Unity per spec).
- Node targets are named rig nodes (`bone`, `socket`, `hinge{axis,limits}`, `wheel{axle}`), so vehicle rigs, gun parts and creature bones are one concept. Attach = `parent` change event (character into seat socket).
- State machine: states (clip, loop mode), transitions (event/guard/min-time), on-enter actions. Triggers come from the ability graph via a `play_effect` / `trigger_motion` action.
- Caps: duration, tracks, keys, particles, live entities, machine states (reuse designer BUDGET semantics).

**Simulator contract:** `sample(spec, state, t) -> Pose + FiredEvents[]` pure and deterministic; `Clock` API (play/pause/seek/scrub, tick rate) exposed by the Model Studio viewport (layers 1-2); three.js adapter maps Pose to Mixer/object transforms; physics (Rapier) only for vehicle dynamics preview, never part of exported truth.

**Exporter contract per game:** `capabilities(game) -> {trackKinds, maxEntities, tickRate, delivery}`; `lower(spec, caps) -> {artifacts, warnings, dropped[]}` so unsupported tracks degrade with an explicit report. Minecraft: transform tracks lower to display-entity interpolation segments, sound/particle cues to scheduler tasks (plugin, within budget), item states to `items/*.json`; creature clips lower to BetterModel `.bbmodel` animation (RigSpec becomes a subset). FiveM adapter later: clip refs to existing dict/name, ptfx refs, door natives.

**Catalog:** presets with kind `motion` / `effect`, per-game support flags, provenance, licence class; AI composes from presets first.

**Ties:** Texture Studio: `light-material` texture-frame track drives `.mcmeta` animated textures and decal swaps; onion-skin already planned. Sound Studio: `sound-cue` references library sound ids; timeline shows waveform with markers snapping to ticks. Model Studio layers 1-2 provide clock and timeline UI; Motion core is the data model both edit.

**Cheapest first slice (end to end):** one item with a gun-state FSM (idle/fire/reload) plus a door prop hinge, in Minecraft display entities + item_model states: spec -> sampler -> three.js preview with scrubber and event log -> exporter emitting plugin-driven display-entity tween + sound cue + `spawn_particles` within existing budgets -> verify on a real 1.21.x and 26.x server. Defer vehicles, BetterModel unification, and non-Minecraft adapters until the core schema survives this slice.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: sbx.sh SCRIPT_BASENAME_IN_work [extra blender args after --]   (runs inside sandbox)
# Mirrors run-capped.sh agents --lock (slice, nice, ionice, oom adj, flock) + extra sandboxing.
set -euo pipefail
W=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/blender-poc
SCRIPT="$1"; shift
exec 7>>/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock
flock -w 1800 7
UNIT=blender-poc-$$
exec systemd-run --quiet --pipe --wait --collect --unit=$UNIT --slice=nxeon-build-agents.slice \
  -p Nice=10 -p IOSchedulingClass=best-effort -p IOSchedulingPriority=7 -p OOMScoreAdjust=1000 \
  -p RuntimeMaxSec=${SBX_MAX:-600} -p KillMode=control-group \
  -p User=nobody -p Group=nogroup \
  -p MemoryMax=4G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p CPUQuota=400% -p TasksMax=256 \
  -p PrivateNetwork=yes -p PrivateTmp=yes -p ProtectSystem=strict -p ProtectHome=tmpfs \
  -p TemporaryFileSystem=/opt:ro -p TemporaryFileSystem=/tank:ro -p TemporaryFileSystem=/mnt:ro -p TemporaryFileSystem=/srv:ro -p TemporaryFileSystem=/var/lib:ro \
  -p TemporaryFileSystem=/etc/pve:ro -p TemporaryFileSystem=/etc/nxeon-build:ro \
  -p BindReadOnlyPaths=$W/blender-5.2.2-linux-x64 -p BindReadOnlyPaths=$W/in \
  -p BindPaths=$W/work -p BindPaths=$W/home \
  -p ProtectKernelTunables=yes -p ProtectKernelModules=yes -p ProtectControlGroups=yes -p ProtectClock=yes \
  -p NoNewPrivileges=yes -p CapabilityBoundingSet= -p RestrictNamespaces=yes -p LockPersonality=yes \
  -p ReadWritePaths=$W/work \
  -p WorkingDirectory=$W/work \
  -E HOME=$W/home -E TMPDIR=/tmp -E LANG=C.UTF-8 -E PATH=/usr/bin:/bin \
  $W/blender-5.2.2-linux-x64/blender --background --factory-startup --python "$W/in/$SCRIPT" "$@"

content.thinking:
I'm planning a Blender script that resets the scene, imports each FBX from the work folder, then organizes every action into its own NLA track per armature so each can be exported as a separate named animation using NLA_TRACKS export mode.

I'll start by testing ACTIONS export mode since it should handle fake-user actions and the newer action-slot system in Blender 5.x, keeping export settings default while noting that Quaternius FBX files may need scale correction. The script itself will just read fixed work/fbx and work/glb directories, running as an unprivileged user with directories pre-created and chowned by root.

input.command:
cat > /tank/cyrus-library-staging/tmp-motion/fbx2glb.py <<'E'
# Deterministic FBX -> glb converter for Blender 5.2 headless. Usage: blender -b --python fbx2glb.py -- [names...]
import bpy, sys, os, json, glob
W='/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/blender-poc/work'
IN=W+'/fbx'; OUT=W+'/glb'
os.makedirs(OUT,exist_ok=True)
args=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--')+1:] if '--' in sys.argv else []
files=sorted(glob.glob(IN+'/*.fbx'))
if args: files=[f for f in files if os.path.basename(f) in args]
report={}
for f in files:
    base=os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0]
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    try:
        bpy.ops.import_scene.fbx(filepath=f)
    except Exception as e:
        report[base]={'error':'import:'+str(e)}; continue
    acts=[a.name for a in bpy.data.actions]
    arms=[o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type=='ARMATURE']
    # park every action as its own NLA track so the exporter writes one clip per FBX stack
    for a in bpy.data.actions: a.use_fake_user=True
    for arm in arms:
        ad=arm.animation_data or arm.animation_data_create()
        ad.action=None
        for a in bpy.data.actions:
            tr=ad.nla_tracks.new(); tr.name=a.name
            st=tr.strips.new(a.name, int(a.frame_range[0]), a)
            st.name=a.name
    out=os.path.join(OUT,base+'.glb')
    try:
        bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=out, export_format='GLB', export_animations=True,
            export_animation_mode='NLA_TRACKS', export_apply=False, export_yup=True,
            export_force_sampling=True, export_optimize_animation_size=False)
        report[base]={'ok':True,'actions':acts,'armatures':len(arms),'size':os.path.getsize(out)}
    except Exception as e:
        report[base]={'error':'export:'+str(e),'actions':acts}
json.dump(report,open(OUT+'/_report.json','w'),indent=1)
print('DONE',len(files))
E

// shares: path/filename tokenising (camelCase, snake_case, Soundminer comma tags, doubled extensions), synonym
// folding through BOTH existing taxonomies (sound + texture) and vocab.json, and the "is this a real content word"
// test that decides stage-A coverage. Pure, client-safe.
import vocabJson from "./vocab.json";
import { TAXONOMY as SOUND_TAX } from "../../sound/classify";
import { TEXTURE_TAXONOMY as TEX_TAX } from "../../texture-library/compile";
import type { CatalogKind } from "./entry";

export type UseForRule = {
  id: string; label: string; kinds: CatalogKind[];
  categoriesAny?: string[]; tagsAny?: string[]; tagsAll?: string[]; useCasesAny?: string[]; stylesAny?: string[];
};
type Vocab = {
  version: number;
  styles: string[];
  styleKeywords: Record<string, string[]>;
  categories: { id: string; keywords: string[] }[];
  categoryAliases: Record<string, string>;
  tags: Record<string, string[]>;
  synonyms: Record<string, string>;
  genericWords: string[];
  useFor: UseForRule[];
  realWorldScale: Record<string, number | string>;
  sourceStyles: Record<string, string[] | string>;
  packStyleHints: Record<string, string>;
};
export const VOCAB = vocabJson as unknown as Vocab;
export const CATEGORY_IDS: readonly string[] = VOCAB.categories.map((c) => c.id);
export const USE_FOR_IDS: readonly string[] = VOCAB.useFor.map((u) => u.id);
export const isCategory = (id: string) => CATEGORY_IDS.includes(id);
export const useForLabel = (id: string) => VOCAB.useFor.find((u) => u.id === id)?.label ?? id;

const GENERIC = new Set(VOCAB.genericWords);
/** raw keyword set (no folding) used to decide whether a plural has a known singular */
const KEYWORDS = (() => {
  const s = new Set<string>();
  for (const c of VOCAB.categories) for (const k of c.keywords) s.add(k);
  for (const list of Object.values(VOCAB.tags)) for (const t of list) s.add(t);
  for (const c of SOUND_TAX.categories) for (const k of c.keywords) s.add(k);
  return s;
})();
export type WordDomain = "audio" | "visual" | "any";
export const canonFor = (domain: WordDomain) => (w: string) => canon(w, domain);
/** canonical form of one word: vocab synonyms, the sound and texture taxonomies' synonym tables, then plural folding to a known singular */
export function canon(w: string, domain: WordDomain = "any"): string {
  // the sound taxonomy's synonyms are about sounds ("mouse" -> click, "steps" -> footsteps) and the texture
  // taxonomy's about pixel items ("bar" -> ingot): each applies only to its own kind of asset
  const syn = VOCAB.synonyms[w] ?? (domain !== "visual" ? SOUND_TAX.synonyms[w] : undefined) ?? (domain !== "audio" ? TEX_TAX.synonyms[w] : undefined);
  if (syn) return syn;
  if (w.length > 3 && w.endsWith("s") && !KEYWORDS.has(w)) {
    for (const sg of [w.endsWith("ies") ? `${w.slice(0, -3)}y` : null, w.endsWith("es") ? w.slice(0, -2) : null, w.slice(0, -1)]) if (sg && KEYWORDS.has(sg)) return sg;
  }
  return w;
}

/** every controlled tag (tag facets + styles + category keywords + both taxonomies' keywords), canonical */
export const CONTROLLED = (() => {
  const s = new Set<string>();
  for (const list of Object.values(VOCAB.tags)) for (const t of list) s.add(t);
  for (const st of VOCAB.styles) s.add(st);
  for (const c of VOCAB.categories) for (const k of c.keywords) s.add(canon(k));
  for (const c of SOUND_TAX.categories) for (const k of c.keywords) s.add(canon(k));
  for (const u of SOUND_TAX.useCases) for (const k of u.keywords) s.add(canon(k));
  for (const c of TEX_TAX.categories) for (const sub of c.subcategories ?? []) for (const k of sub.keywords ?? []) s.add(canon(k));
  for (const u of VOCAB.useFor) for (const t of [...(u.tagsAny ?? []), ...(u.tagsAll ?? [])]) s.add(t);
  return s;
})();
export const isControlled = (t: string) => CONTROLLED.has(t);

/** split camelCase / PascalCase / letter-digit boundaries: "playerBlue_duck" -> "player Blue duck", "Metal033" -> "Metal 033" */
const splitCase = (s: string) => s.replace(/([a-z])([A-Z])/g, "$1 $2").replace(/([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/g, "$1 $2").replace(/([A-Za-z])(\d)/g, "$1 $2").replace(/(\d)([A-Za-z])/g, "$1 $2");
export const stripExt = (name: string) => name.replace(/(\.(mp3|wav|aif|aiff|ogg|flac|png|jpg|jpeg|glb|gltf|hdr|exr|webp|mtlx|usdc|blend))+$/i, "");

/** raw lowercase words of a string (no synonym folding), digits kept as their own tokens */
export function words(s: string): string[] {

"""Deterministic procedural flipbook toolkit (numpy + PIL only). Everything is seeded; same seed = same bytes."""
import numpy as np, json, os, hashlib
from PIL import Image

f32 = np.float32

def smooth(a, b, x):
    t = np.clip((x - a) / (b - a), 0, 1)
    return t * t * (3 - 2 * t)

# ---------- noise ----------
def noise3(Y, X, T, cells, seed, salt=0):
    """Periodic 3D value noise. Y,X,T broadcastable arrays in cell units, lattice period = cells (cy,cx,ct)."""
    cy, cx, ct = [int(c) for c in cells]
    L = np.random.default_rng([int(seed), int(salt)]).random((cy, cx, ct), dtype=f32)
    def idx(c, n):
        i0 = np.floor(c).astype(np.int64)
        f = (c - i0).astype(f32)

import json, sys, os, glob
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

def frames_of(path, side):
    im = Image.open(path).convert('RGBA'); sc = json.load(open(path[:-4] + '.json'))
    F = sc['frameSize']; cols = sc['grid'][0]; n = sc['frames']
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        r, c = divmod(i, cols)
        out.append(im.crop((c * F, r * F, (c + 1) * F, (r + 1) * F)))
    return sc, out

def make(paths, out, thumb=84, per_row=8, per_page=18, title=''):
    pages = [paths[i:i + per_page] for i in range(0, len(paths), per_page)]
    for pi, pg in enumerate(pages):
        W = 190 + per_row * (thumb + 2); H = len(pg) * (thumb + 2) + 4
        canvas = Image.new('RGB', (W, H), (20, 22, 30)); d = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
        for ri, p in enumerate(pg):

            idx = np.linspace(0, len(fr) - 1, min(per_row, len(fr))).round().astype(int)
            d.text((4, ri * (thumb + 2) + 6), os.path.basename(p)[:-4][:34], fill=(220, 220, 230))
            d.text((4, ri * (thumb + 2) + 22), f"{sc['frames']}f {sc['frameSize']}px {sc['blend']}", fill=(140, 150, 170))
            add = sc['blend'] in ('additive', 'screen')
            bg = (14, 16, 24) if add else (96, 100, 108)
            if sc['blend'] == 'opaque': bg = (0, 0, 0)
            for k, i in enumerate(idx):
                f = fr[i].resize((thumb, thumb), Image.LANCZOS)
                a = np.asarray(f).astype(np.float32) / 255
                base = np.zeros((thumb, thumb, 3), np.float32) + np.array(bg, np.float32) / 255
                if add: res = base + a[..., :3] * a[..., 3:4]
                else: res = base * (1 - a[..., 3:4]) + a[..., :3] * a[..., 3:4]
                canvas.paste(Image.fromarray((np.clip(res, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)), (190 + k * (thumb + 2), ri * (thumb + 2) + 2))
        fn = out if len(pages) == 1 else out.replace('.png', f'-{pi + 1}.png')
        canvas.save(fn)
        print(fn)

    make(sorted(glob.glob(sys.argv[1] + '/*.png')), sys.argv[2])

import json, sys, os, glob

def make(paths, out, thumb=84, per_row=8, per_page=18, title=''):
    pages = [paths[i:i + per_page] for i in range(0, len(paths), per_page)]
    for pi, pg in enumerate(pages):

content.thinking:
The ring effect feels too dominant compared to the spokes, so I'm reducing its default size and lengthening the star spokes so they extend past the ring instead of hiding inside it—maybe even letting some variants drop the ring entirely. The muzzle shape looks fine from the front and side angles.

Sparks are too small, sparse, and disappear too fast, so I'm scaling up their speed, size, count, and lifetime so they travel and fade more naturally. The splash effect also feels weak—I'm boosting jet height, droplet speed and size, and overall power so it reads as a real impact. Dust currently looks like one blob rather than distinct puffs, so I'm increasing spread and shrinking individual puff size to make them more discrete and turbulent-looking.

For embers, I want them rising rather than clustering at the bottom, so I'm narrowing the emission cone upward, giving them negative gravity for lift, and tuning origin, speed, and lifetime accordingly. Once these adjustments feel right, I'll bake them into the defaults.

For the aura ring, I'm using periodic polar noise so the rotation loops seamlessly, and the orb gets a pulsating glow core with swirling halo noise and orbiting sparkle particles. Now I'm sketching out the rune circle with concentric rotating rings.

For the heal pillar I'll add rising ring bands with a cosine wave moving upward. For the portal effect, I'm thinking of a swirling spiral with a darker center disc and glowing edges, using arm count and radial log functions for the swirl intensity. For the bubble shield I'll use a fresnel-style rim glow with faint fill and sparkle noise, and for electric effects I'm sketching a bolt function that uses midpoint displacement to generate jagged lightning paths.

Now I'm working out rendering: picking a random seed per frame, drawing a main bolt plus a few branching bolts from random points with angle offsets, using dense polyline sampling with a tight core blur and wider colored glow blur. I'm also planning a Tesla-ball variant with tendrils radiating from a center point to random points on a ring, and considering different bolt styles like vertical, horizontal, diagonal, and ball variants.

For the rain effect, I'm working out how to make looping streaks tileable by choosing slant and speed values so the horizontal drift lines up to an integer multiple of the frame width over one loop cycle.

I'm figuring out how to tile the rain streaks seamlessly by drawing duplicate copies offset by the frame width and wrapping sample positions with modulo, then layering multiple depth bands with different integer-loop speeds and brightness for parallax. For snow, I'm planning soft gaussian-blob flakes that fall with periodic sine drift for a swaying motion, varying blur and brightness by depth, plus considering a dark slow-rising ember variant for ash. Then I start sketching a tileable animated water texture using periodic noise for height and a caustics pattern derived from it.

Now I'm working out the water normal map by taking finite differences of the periodic height field to build surface normals, then moving to a lava tile using animated Worley/cellular noise with feature points orbiting in loops to stay seamless, blended with cracks and a crust-to-yellow color ramp, and finally adapting the fire function into a horizontally tileable wall variant by widening its core profile.

I realize the asymmetric width-based falloff breaks tileability, so I switch to a dedicated firewall function that derives intensity purely from vertical life/height falloff plus periodic noise and turbulence, keeping it horizontally tileable while treating the vertical axis as non-looping. """Families C: magic auras, electric arcs, rain/snow, tileable liquids, slash arcs."""

COLS = {'blue': (.3, .55, 1), 'purple': (.65, .35, 1), 'green': (.3, 1, .5), 'gold': (1, .8, .25), 'red': (1, .25, .2), 'cyan': (.2, .95, 1), 'pink': (1, .4, .8), 'white': (1, 1, 1), 'orange': (1, .55, .15)}
def mag_ramp(col):

    return [(0, *(c * .5), 0), (.12, *(c * .7), .15), (.4, *c, .75), (.75, *(c * .5 + w * .5), .97), (1, 1, 1, 1, 1)]

def _polar(F):
    Y, X = _coords(F)
    dx = X - 0.5; dy = Y - 0.5
    return np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) + 1e-5, np.arctan2(dy, dx)

def _sparkles(F, t, rng_state, n, region, col_w=1.0, rise=0.0, orbit=None):
    """periodic sparkles: returns (F,F) canvas. positions are functions of phase so loops are seamless"""

    else:

def magic(F, T, seed, style='ring', col='blue', R=0.33, width=0.05, arms=3, sparkles=20, poly=0, spin=1, turb=1.0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    r, a = _polar(F)
    Y, X = _coords(F)
    stops = mag_ramp(col)
    sp_state = (rng.random(sparkles), rng.random(sparkles), rng.random(sparkles), 0.7 + rng.random(sparkles) * 1.2)
    out = np.zeros((T, F, F, 4), f32)
    for i in range(T):
        t = i / T
        ang = (a / 6.2832 + 0.5)
        if style == 'ring':
            n = fbm(r * 6, ang * 6 + t * 6 * spin, np.full_like(r, t) * 2 , (6, 6, 2), seed, 3, 0.5, 1)
            env = np.exp(-((r - R * (1 + 0.03 * np.sin(6.2832 * t))) / width) ** 2)
            h = env * (0.4 + 1.1 * n * turb) + np.exp(-((r - R) / (width * 3.5)) ** 2) * 0.22
            inner = np.exp(-(r / (R * 0.9)) ** 4) * 0.12
            h = np.clip(h + inner, 0, 1)
            sp = _sparkles(F, t, sp_state, sparkles, None, orbit=(R, 1, 0.5))
            h = np.clip(h + sp * 0.9, 0, 1)
        elif style == 'orb':
            pulse = 1 + 0.10 * np.sin(6.2832 * t)

            halo = np.exp(-(r / (R * 1.1)) ** 2) * (0.35 + 0.6 * n * turb)

            h = np.clip(prof * (0.35 + 0.5 * bands) * (0.6 + 0.6 * n * turb) + np.exp(-(wx / (R * 0.9)) ** 2) * 0.12 * smooth(0, 0.1, v), 0, 1)
            # base glow disc
            h = np.maximum(h, np.exp(-((wx / (R * 1.0)) ** 2 + ((Y - 0.9) / 0.04) ** 2)) * 0.9)
            ph, x0, y0, sz = sp_state
            c = np.zeros((F, F), np.float64)

        elif style == 'bubble':
            fres = np.clip((r / R), 0, 1.5) ** 5 * smooth(R * 1.04, R * 0.97, r)
            rim = np.exp(-((r - R) / (width * 0.5)) ** 2)
            n = fbm(Y * 4, X * 4, np.full_like(Y, t) * 2 + 0 * X, (4, 4, 2), seed, 3, 0.5, 1)
            hexp = 0.5 + 0.5 * np.cos(6.2832 * (X * 9 + Y * 5 + t)) * np.cos(6.2832 * (Y * 9 - X * 3 - t))

def _bolt(rng, p0, p1, disp, depth):
    pts = [p0, p1]

            m = (a + b) / 2; v = b - a; L = np.hypot(*v) + 1e-6
            nrm = np.array([-v[1], v[0]]) / L
            m = m + nrm * (rng.random() - 0.5) * 2 * disp * L
            new += [m, b]
        pts = new; disp *= 0.62
    return np.array(pts)

def electric(F, T, seed, style='bolt', col='blue', branches=3, disp=0.22, glow=2.6, width=1.0, tendrils=7):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

        if style in ('bolt', 'horizontal', 'diagonal'):

    """tileable looping precipitation. all motion is an integer number of tile wraps per loop."""

            else:

def _worley(F, cells, t, seed, loops=1):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

            n = fbm(Y * scale + t * flow * scale, X * scale, np.full_like(Y, t) * 2 + 0 * X, (scale, scale, 2), seed, 4, 0.5, 3)
            h = np.clip(0.18 + 0.55 * crack + 0.45 * n ** 2 + 0.15 * (1 - d1) , 0, 1) * 0.95 + 0.0
            h = np.clip(h * (0.55 + 0.9 * (1 - np.clip((d2 - d1) * 3.2, 0, 1))), 0, 1)
            out[i] = ramp(h, pals[pal])
    return out

def firewall(F, T, seed, pal='fire', h=1.0, sway=1.0, turb=0.7, cx=4, cy=4, cyc=1, post=0):
    Y, X = _coords(F)
    out = np.zeros((T, F, F, 4), f32)
    v = 1 - Y
    for i in range(T):
        t = i / T
        n1 = fbm(Y * cy + t * cyc * cy, X * cx, np.full_like(Y, t) * 2 + 0 * X, (cy, cx, 2), seed, 4, 0.5, 1)
        n2 = fbm((Y * cy + t * cyc * cy) * 2, X * cx * 2, np.full_like(Y, t) * 4 + 0 * X, (cy * 2, cx * 2, 4), seed, 3, 0.5, 2)
        base = (1 - v / h) * 1.35 + (n1 - 0.5) * sway * 1.3 - (1 - n2) * turb * (v / h) * 0.9
        inten = np.clip(base, 0, 1)
        if post: inten = np.floor(inten * post + .5) / post
        out[i] = ramp(inten, RAMPS[pal])
    return out

def slash(F, T, seed, col='white', span=2.3, R=0.36, thick=0.075, rot=-0.6, flip=1, tail=0.7):
    r, a = _polar(F)
    stops = mag_ramp(col)
    out = np.zeros((T, F, F, 4), f32)
    for i in range(T):
        t = (i + 0.5) / T
        th = ((a - rot) * flip + 3.1416) % 6.2832 - 3.1416  # angle relative to arc centre
        head = -span / 2 + span * smooth(0.0, 0.75, t) * 1.0
        tailp = head - span * tail * (0.35 + 0.65 * smooth(0.0, 0.5, t))
        inwin = smooth(tailp, tailp + span * 0.2, th) * (1 - smooth(head - 0.02, head + 0.02, th)) * (np.abs(th) < span / 2 + 0.05)
        taper = np.clip(np.cos(np.clip(th / (span / 2 + 1e-3), -1, 1) * 1.5708), 0, 1) ** 0.8
        along = np.clip((th - tailp) / (head - tailp + 1e-4), 0, 1)
        Rr = R * (1 + 0.04 * np.sin(th * 2))
        wid = thick * taper * (0.35 + 0.65 * along) * (1.0 + 0.5 * t)
        prof = np.exp(-((r - Rr) / np.maximum(wid, 1e-3)) ** 2)
        h = np.clip(prof * inwin * along ** 0.6 * 1.25 * np.clip(1.5 - t, 0, 1), 0, 1)
        out[i] = ramp(h, stops)
    return out

content.thinking:
The electric effect needs thicker, glowier lines with a brighter centered core glow, so I should increase the core sigma and gain for more brightness. The water effect looks a bit too much like lightning caustics, but is otherwise fine.

For the firewall, the white areas are blowing out too much, so I need to scale the base down and tune the gain to avoid saturation. The rain effect is too faint on grey, so I should boost density, alpha, and splat weights to make the streaks more visible. The slash effect reads fine as a sweeping crescent, and rain tiles are seamless by design.

Before writing the production generator with parameter variations, I want to verify that explosion and fire loops are truly seamless by adding a deterministic QA metric comparing the last frame to the first frame relative to average consecutive frame differences, expecting a ratio near 1 for proper loops. Now I'm moving on to the production script.

I'm planning out the full spec list: fire variants (campfire, candle, torch, inferno, toon, magic colors, lava, firewall, embers) across different sizes and frame counts, plus smoke variants (plume, puff, steam) and explosion types (fire, plasma, toon, dust, toxic, shockwave) with their respective size and style combinations to total roughly 30+ fire assets and similar counts for smoke and explosions.

Now I'm sketching out water effects — splash tints (water, deep, lava, slime, milk, toxic, ice) and ripple styles (single-ring, multi-ring, foam, ellipse, drop) across sizes, aiming for around 26 total water assets, and I'm about to move into planning the sparks/burst category next.

Then for sparks I'm counting burst colors (fire, white, blue, green, gold, purple, steel), fountains, and ember loops across sizes to land near 23 variants; muzzle flashes break into front/side/shotgun/pistol shapes with spike counts and colors for roughly 20; dust gets brown/grey/sand/snow tones across sizes for about 10; impact effects (star, spark, comic, ringburst, frost) across colors give around 15; and magic effects split into ring, orb, rune, portal, and pillar styles across color sets, picking a manageable subset from the full 48 possibilities.

Electric effects add bolts, horizontal/diagonal variants, balls, and chains for about 18; slashes across colors and flip variants give 8; rain, snow, and steam combos add 12; and liquids (water types, lava, magma) across resolutions give 16. Adding everything up puts the total around 275 variants, comfortably past the 150 target, and I'm now checking disk size and generation time feasibility for 256px sheets with multi-frame fbm noise, estimating render time per explosion and total batch time.

Memory per array stays modest (~8MB with fbm temp buffers around 100MB), so I'm now planning the tagging system — deterministic tags combining family, style, color, size descriptor, loop flag, and category metadata for discovery. I'm also setting per-family fps standards (fire at 20fps, explosions at 30fps, muzzle flashes at 30fps) and designing a table-driven generator where each entry specifies family, name, function, parameters, frame count, duration, blend mode, loop behavior, fps, tags, and a deterministic seed derived from a CRC32 hash of the name. I want the pipeline to be resumable, skipping entries whose PNG and JSON already exist unless forced, logging generation time, and computing a seam metric for looping sheets to verify smooth wraparound.

- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

import sys, re, time, subprocess, json, os, html, zipfile, urllib.parse

    lm = re.search(r'Asset license\s+(.{0,70}?)\s+(Content|Download|Links|Author|Tags|Price)', txt)
    lic = lm.group(1).strip() if lm else ''
    ds = re.search(r'LICENSE?:?\s*(.{0,200})', txt, re.I)
    tt = re.search(r'<title>(.*?)</title>', t); title = html.unescape(tt.group(1)) if tt else slug

    except Exception: meta['status'] = 'FAIL download_url: ' + j[:100]; json.dump(meta, open(d + '/_meta.json', 'w')); print(url, meta['status']); continue
    pg = run([dl]); time.sleep(6)
    ups = re.findall(r'data-upload_id="(\d+)"', pg)
    names = re.findall(r'class="upload_name"[^>]*>.*?title="([^"]+)"', pg, re.S)
    key = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlparse(dl).query).get('key', [None])[0] or dl.rstrip('/').split('/')[-1]
    meta['uploads'] = []
    csrf2 = re.search(r'name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)"', pg)
    for i, uid in enumerate(dict.fromkeys(ups)):

        fn = os.path.join(d, re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+', '_', (names[i] if i < len(names) else f'upload{uid}')))
        if run([cdn], fn): print('FAIL dl', uid); continue
        meta['uploads'].append(os.path.basename(fn))
        if zipfile.is_zipfile(fn):
            try: zipfile.ZipFile(fn).extractall(fn + '_x')
            except Exception as e: print('zip err', e)
            os.remove(fn)
        time.sleep(6)
    meta['status'] = 'downloaded' if meta['uploads'] else 'FAIL no uploads'
    json.dump(meta, open(d + '/_meta.json', 'w')); print(url, '|', lic, '|', meta['status'], meta['uploads'], flush=True)

With determinism confirmed, I'm thinking about expanding further into procedural glTF animation clips for simple mechanisms, like a door hinge rotating open and closed, since these can be generated deterministically without licensing concerns.

I'm sketching out a pure-Python glTF writer that builds box meshes with materials, hierarchical pivot nodes, and animation tracks sampled from easing curves at 30fps, then planning a script, mechgen.py, to define reusable parts and assemble assets like a door-hinge model with a frame and swinging door.

I'm expanding the asset list to cover double-doors, sliding doors, trapdoors, drawers, chests, levers, buttons, pressure plates, pistons, gears, wheels, fans, windmills, turntables, elevators, and drawbridges, plus a full vehicle rig with four doors, hood, trunk, spinning wheels, and front-wheel steering animations.

Then I'm covering weapon props like a pistol with slide, hammer, and magazine actions, a rifle bolt cycle, pump-action shotgun, and revolver cylinder rotation, considering embedding event markers (fire, reload, cock, slide) via glTF extras. I'm also listing misc props like bobbing pickups, pulsing scales, swinging signs and lanterns, pendulums, and treasure chest pops, deciding to skip flags, blinking lights, and conveyors for now.

Clips are authored as keyframe tracks sampled at 30fps with linear interpolation, rotations pre-sampled via quaternion slerp. Given this covers door mechanisms and gun cocking explicitly requested, I'm building this out as a mechanism script that writes GLB files — generating box meshes with baked-in part dimensions and local pivots, basic PBR materials, and a node/animation builder that assembles named nodes with parent hierarchies, transforms, and keyframe tracks.

Still writing animation sampling and easing logic...

Each track stores keyed node transforms with euler rotation converted to quaternion, and animations fully override a node's local transform for the affected channel. I'm now planning to generate each asset as its own glb file under motion/procedural-motion/, with every node and animation bundled inside.

Roughly 40 glbs with around 150 total clips across them, each glb holding one animated model plus its associated animation clips. For doors I'm setting up a static frame of three boxes with a hinge pivot node offset to the door edge so rotation about Y swings the door open; for the gun I'm rigging separate parts (frame, slide, hammer, trigger, magazine) with translate/rotate channels to build fire and cock animation clips.

For reload animations I'm sequencing magazine removal, a pause, then reinsertion and slide release, and adding similar bolt/pump/cylinder mechanics for rifles, shotguns, and revolvers, plus muzzle-flash event markers in the extras data. About 30 of 140 OGA items are done so far; I should check the reject count and let it continue while I prep the itch queue in parallel. I'm now planning a generic external ingest cataloger that scans new directories under opengameart and itch, handling image file types.

It needs to detect frame sequences from numbered filenames, sprite sheets via grid detection, static particle textures, and animated GIFs using frame counts, plus handle 3D model formats like GLB/GLTF/FBX, converting FBX via Blender and skipping static-only formats like DAE/OBJ. I'll dedupe everything by sha256 against the main catalog and prior passes, and derive tags from the slug tokens.

For each entry I need to classify effect category from normalized tokens, falling back to a low-confidence 'vfx/particles' bucket when empty, while skipping junk files like tiny or preview assets. I'm deciding to keep ambiguous sprites (like mixed asset packs) as flipbook/particle-texture rather than filtering too aggressively, only excluding clearly non-effect items like icons or tilesets, and pulling licensing fields (SPDX, tier, attribution, source) straight from each pack's metadata file.

I also need deduplication via file hashing against already-seen IDs, and a plan for animated 3D models: GLBs get cataloged directly while FBX files get queued for a Blender conversion pass before cataloging. I'm going to write this ingestion logic now as s5_ingest.py, including the FBX-to-do tracking, and test it once real data is available.

import sys, os, json, glob, csv, re, collections

for l in open('/tank/cyrus-library-staging/catalog.jsonl'): main_ids.add(json.loads(l)['id'])
p1 = {}
for l in open(M + '/catalog-motion.jsonl'): p1[json.loads(l)['id']] = 1
rows = []; seen = set(); drop = collections.Counter()
HEX = re.compile(r'^[0-9a-f]{64}$')
for pf in sorted(glob.glob(M + '/parts/*.jsonl')):
    for l in open(pf):
        r = json.loads(l)
        if not HEX.match(r['id']): drop['bad-id'] += 1; continue
        if r['id'] in seen: drop['dup-in-run'] += 1; continue
        if r['id'] in main_ids and r['kind'] in ('flipbook', 'particle-texture'): drop['in-main-catalog'] += 1; continue
        if r['id'] in p1: drop['in-pass1'] += 1; continue
        if r.get('tier') != 'cc0' or r.get('attribution') is not None or r.get('licenseSpdx') != 'CC0-1.0': drop['NOT-CC0'] += 1; raise SystemExit('licence rule violated: ' + r['path'])
        seen.add(r['id']); rows.append(r)
write_rows(CAT2, rows)
print('rows', len(rows), dict(collections.Counter(r['kind'] for r in rows)), 'dropped', dict(drop))
# ledger

L.append(['nxeon-procedural', 'authored mechanism/prop/gun/vehicle clips (glb)', 'CC0-1.0, authored by Nxeon', 'motion/tools2/s2b_mech.py', TODAY, 'ACCEPT cc0', 'we authored; gltf-validator 0 errors / 0 warnings'])
for mp in sorted(glob.glob(M + '/opengameart/*/_meta.json')):
    m = json.load(open(mp))
    if m['slug'] in set(json.load(open(M + '/_old_oga_slugs.json'))): continue
    if m.get('tier') == 'cc0': L.append(['opengameart', m['slug'], 'License(s): ' + m['lic'], m['url'], TODAY, 'ACCEPT cc0' if m.get('status') == 'downloaded' else 'ACCEPT cc0 (download issue)', m.get('status', '')])
    else: L.append(['opengameart', m['slug'], 'License(s): ' + m['lic'], m['url'], TODAY, 'REJECT', 'not exactly CC0 (multi-licence or attribution licence); dual-licence pages held for owner, never used'])
for mp in sorted(glob.glob(M + '/itch/*/_meta.json')):
    m = json.load(open(mp))

    L.append(['itch.io', f"{m['user']}/{m['slug']}", 'Asset license: ' + (m.get('assetLicenseField') or 'none shown'), m['url'], TODAY, 'ACCEPT cc0' if ok and m.get('status') == 'downloaded' else 'REJECT/FAIL', m.get('status', '')])

L.append(['kenney.nl', 'remaining packs', 'CC0', 'https://kenney.nl/assets', TODAY, 'N/A', 'all Kenney packs with motion/particles already staged in pass 1 (Particle Pack, Smoke Particles, Splat Pack, Light Masks) or by the 3D ingest'])

I'll detect sequences by finding files in a directory sharing a stem prefix with trailing integers (at least 4 files), then represent each group as a single row with an id derived from hashing the sorted file hashes together, plus frame count and size info.
